report:
## Conclusion

Yes, treatment with corticosteroids such as dexamethasone has been shown to improve survival in critically ill COVID-19 patients, though it does not guarantee survival and is most effective in those with severe disease requiring oxygen or ventilatory support.

The landmark **RECOVERY trial** (published in NEJM, July 2020) demonstrated that dexamethasone at 6 mg daily for up to 10 days reduced 28-day mortality by 17% overall (rate ratio 0.83, p=0.0007), with the greatest benefit seen in patients requiring invasive mechanical ventilation. The benefit was significant for patients receiving either oxygen alone or mechanical ventilation, but not for those not requiring respiratory support.

This finding was reinforced by the **WHO REACT Working Group prospective meta-analysis** (published in JAMA, September 2020), which pooled data from seven randomized trials and found that systemic corticosteroid administration was associated with lower 28-day all-cause mortality among critically ill COVID-19 patients. Based on this evidence, the **WHO issued guidance** recommending corticosteroids for severe and critical COVID-19 cases.

However, timing matters: corticosteroids given too early in the disease course (within 7 days of symptom onset) showed no mortality benefit and could potentially weaken innate immunity. The evidence supports use specifically in hospitalized patients with severe respiratory complications, not in mild or early-stage disease.
